stemBlocks.value: Make h the subject of the formula A = bh/2 (the area of a triangle).
Think first: Clear the fraction first, then deal with what is left multiplying h.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q05 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the denominator.
Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply both sides by 2 to remove the denominator, then divide by b.

whyThisWorks.value: Dividing by 2 and multiplying by b are the two operations applied to h, so undoing them in reverse order — multiply by 2 first, then divide by b — releases h. Clearing the fraction before dividing keeps the working tidy and avoids stacked fractions.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by b before clearing the fraction and producing a messy compound fraction.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by b before clearing the fraction and producing a messy compound fraction.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing h = A/(2b) by multiplying the denominator by 2 instead of the numerator.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing h = A/(2b) by multiplying the denominator by 2 instead of the numerator.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting that 2 multiplies A, not b.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting that 2 multiplies A, not b.

examTip.value: When a formula contains a fraction, multiply through by the denominator as your very first move — every later step is then fraction-free.
